name: norm_sieve_execution

phase_0.boundary_condition: the upper limit of the search space defined by the sieve range

VINIT.justification: the state before the sieve array is initialized or populated with integers

TANCH.justification: the final boundary that terminates the execution once the limit is reached

AFWD.justification: the forward movement to the next integer in the sequence

AREV.justification: the return to a previous state to re-evaluate or adjust the step size

CLINK.justification: the sequential application of the marking operation to multiples of a prime

IMSCRIB.justification: the verification that a number is being compared against its own primality status

FSPLIT.justification: the division of a candidate integer into either a prime path or a composite path

FFUSE.justification: the merging of prime and composite classifications back into the unified result set

EVALT.justification: the affirmative state where a number is identified as prime

EVALF.justification: the negative state where a number is identified as composite

ENGAGR.justification: the state of a number before the sieve reaches its multiples where it is both potentially prime and potentially composite

IFIX.justification: the permanent and irreversible recording of the primality status in the output buffer

phase_3.void_description: the null state of the sieve array before memory allocation
phase_3.true_description: the bit flag representing a prime number
phase_3.false_description: the bit flag representing a composite number
phase_3.both_description: the unvisited state where a number is not yet processed by the sieve logic

steps.domain_action: allocate memory for the sieve array and initialize all values to the unvisited state
identify the starting integer as the first candidate for evaluation
branch the execution based on whether the current integer is already marked as composite
enter the composite branch if the integer is a multiple of a previously found prime
return to the main loop to skip further processing for this composite number
rejoin the execution flow to proceed to the next candidate
branch the execution for an unmarked integer to perform a primality test
enter the prime branch when the integer is confirmed as prime
move forward to calculate the multiples of this newly found prime
chain the marking operations to flag every multiple of the prime as composite
record the prime status permanently in the result table
rejoin the execution flow after marking all multiples
check if the current pointer has reached the terminal boundary
branch based on the boundary check result
continue the loop if the limit is not yet reached
increment the pointer to the next integer
return to the start of the evaluation cycle
enter the termination branch if the limit is reached
close the sieve execution and release the result table

phase_5.compiler_frontend: the sieve algorithm logic that maps mathematical primality to bitwise operations
phase_5.ipc_mechanism: the memory bus that transfers flags between the processing unit and the sieve array
phase_5.memory_mechanism: the bit-mapped array storing the primality status of each integer
phase_5.scheduler_mechanism: the loop controller that manages the iteration over the integer range
phase_5.alfs_store: the fundamental theorem of arithmetic which dictates the sieve logic

phase_6.cycle_cost: the CPU cycles and memory bandwidth required to mark a single composite number
phase_6.pre_cycle_state: an array of unvisited integers with unknown primality
phase_6.post_cycle_state: a fully classified array of primes and composites
phase_6.delta_s_verdict: ΔS ≈ 0 — the information gained about primality is exactly equal to the reduction in the state space of the array
